chunks: What a microcontroller timer is. The question: What are timers in a microcontroller?
A microcontroller timer is a hardware counter that adds one on every tick of a clock. It runs on its own, without the processor doing anything.
When the count reaches a number you chose, or wraps around to zero, the hardware can set a flag (a status bit), signal the processor, flip a pin, or restart itself.
That gives you exact timing while the processor does other work.
Picture a tap dripping steadily into a measuring cup. Each drip is one clock tick, and the water level is the count. You paint a fill line on the cup.
When the water reaches it, a bell rings, and a siphon empties the cup so it can start again. While the cup fills, you are free to do other jobs.

The clock goes through a divider into a counter; comparators watch for the match value and the reload value, and each can produce a pin change, a flag, an interrupt or a trigger to another peripheral.
Counter: the storage that holds the current count and goes up by one each tick. Tick: one step of the counter. It is the smallest time the timer can resolve.
Prescaler: a divider before the counter that slows the clock, so longer times fit in the counter. Compare or reload value: the number the counter is checked against.
A match sets a flag or restarts the counter. Interrupt: a signal that makes the processor pause its work and respond to the timer.
A chip runs at 16 megahertz. A prescaler that divides by 16 gives a 1 megahertz tick, which is one tick per microsecond. Let the counter run from 0 to 999 and then restart.
That is 1000 counts, so the timer produces an event every 1 milliseconds, a 1 kilohertz rate.
Note the off-by-one: the counter includes 0, so a reload value of 999 gives 1000 counts, not 999. The timing stays exact however busy the main program is. That is the whole idea.
"A timer is a hardware counter that counts clock ticks independently of the CPU.
A prescaler slows the clock, and a compare or reload register tells it when to raise a flag, fire an interrupt, or toggle a pin.
So with 16 megahertz and a prescaler of 16 I get a 1 megahertz tick, and counting to 1000 gives me an exact 1 milliseconds event regardless of what the code is doing.
The same hardware is used for PWM, measuring pulse widths with input capture, and scheduler ticks."
Quick check. What is a microcontroller timer, at its core?
